title: Progressive trust ladder
lede: A personal agent climbs four rungs as risk and amount rise: sign-in, step-up, then a CIBA approval on a phone. MOCK: simulated, no tenant.

nodes.label: Customer
sub: Taps sign in, step up, or pay. Never sees a redirect.

nodes.label: Personal agent
sub: Shows the rung, the reason and the trace.

nodes.label: Ladder core
sub: Checks each proof: acr, auth_time, jti, window.

nodes.label: Mock proofs
sub: Server-minted MOCK sign-in and step-up events.

nodes.label: CIBA store
sub: Holds the backchannel request. Single use.

nodes.label: Mock phone
sub: The only way to approve or deny.

steps.title: Sign in: rung 0 to rung 1
steps.what: The customer signs in. The server mints a MOCK sign-in proof and the ladder raises the rung once.
steps.why: A proof raises one rung, and its jti is single use.

steps.title: Step-up: rung 1 to rung 2
steps.what: A fresh MOCK step-up proof (acr mock:multi) satisfies the in-app check.
steps.why: Step-up is needed for payments above 300. A proof older than 300 s is refused.

steps.title: Refused below rung 3
steps.what: A payment of 800 needs rung 3. The ladder refuses it with rung_required and names the rung needed.
steps.why: Risk and amount never lower a rung; they only raise what is needed.

steps.title: CIBA: the phone decides
steps.what: The agent asks for an approval. Only the mock phone can approve or deny it.
steps.why: The requester has no decide method; the approver is a separate handle.

steps.title: Approved payment: approval consumed
steps.what: The agent polls once, rung 3 is reached, the payment goes through and the single-use approval is spent: rung 2 again.
steps.why: Each CIBA approval pays one amount, once.
